chunks: I would love it if there were a Mushaf (Quran) in the house by which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, repels the devils.

key_terms.الشَّيَاطِين: Al-shayatin — the devils, plural of Shaytan; refers to Iblis and the demonic jinn who mislead humans
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Azza wa jalla — 'Mighty and Majestic', a formula of glorification applied to God, distinguishing divine majesty
key_terms.مُصْحَف: Mushaf — the physical written copy of the Quran, from the root s-h-f (pages/scrolls); distinct from Quran as recited text

ai.seo_question: Does keeping a Quran in the house protect against devils according to Islamic hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) expressed his love for having the Quran physically present in the home, stating that Allah repels the devils through its presence. This teaching reflects the understanding that the Quran is not merely a text for recitation but also carries a protective spiritual power. In early Muslim practice, keeping a physical copy of the Quran in the home was seen as a means of divine protection and barakah (blessing).
